subject: art-and-design
topicName: Design Principles Balance Emphasis Proportion Unity Variety Rhythm

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Balance: symmetrical (formal, stable), asymmetrical (dynamic, informal), radial (centred, expansive). Emphasis: creating a focal point through contrast, position or isolation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Proportion: the size relationship between parts — can be realistic or deliberately distorted for effect. Unity: coherence through consistent style, colour or motif.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Variety: visual interest through contrast, difference and change — prevents monotony. Rhythm: regular, flowing or progressive repetition that creates movement.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Design principles work TOGETHER — a composition balances unity and variety, uses emphasis within proportion, creates rhythm through balance.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to design principles balance emphasis proportion unity variety rhythm, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development f | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
